backlog.description: Add an idea or TODO to docs/agents/backlog
backlog.template:
Add a note to `docs/agents/backlog/` for the idea below, following `docs/agents/backlog/README.md`
and the template `docs/agents/templates/backlog.md`. Check existing notes first and extend one
instead of duplicating it. Do not implement anything and do not create a branch or commit — just
write the note and show its path.

$ARGUMENTS

dispatch.description: Dispatch topics for worker-local discussion, planning and implementation
dispatch.template:
Act as the dispatcher from `docs/agents/protocols/parallel.md` exactly, for these topics:

$ARGUMENTS


Before recommending or launching topics, follow Protocol parallel's freshness check: fetch
origin successfully and triage the fetched `origin/master` revision. A fetch alone does not
refresh checkout files; do not use a stale local backlog or redispatch notes removed upstream.

Use the session-host selection in Protocol parallel. In Orca, `worker.py start --host auto`
launches a visible Orca worker in the shared-script worktree, following Chat/CLI preference.
Keep repository lifecycle status authoritative across Orca assignment completion and approval
pauses; resume and cleanup must use the recorded Orca identities. Do not launch a second
backend-native worker as a fallback. Require an exact workspace selector for ambiguous checkouts.

For backend-hosted workers, a successful launch must also pass the native session visibility checks in Protocol parallel.
Codex workers are independent interactive tasks on the shared app-server daemon and appear in
`codex agents`; do not launch them with `codex exec` or describe them as parent-owned subagents.
Claude workers appear in `claude agents`; OpenCode workers use the UI's shared session service.
Report the worker names and how to open their existing conversations for requirements and review.
Select only the initial planning backend/model and respect explicit developer preferences. The
planner revisits implementation selection with the completed plan; continuing its session is
the default. Requirements, scope decisions and approvals go directly to the developer in that
worker conversation, never through a dispatcher relay. Report which worker needs attention and
how to open it; handle assignment problems, overlapping edits and shared resources here.

implement.description: Implement an approved plan following docs/agents/protocols/implement.md
implement.template:
Follow `docs/agents/protocols/implement.md` exactly for the plan:

For a registered worker, require explicit plan approval in this worker session or a validated,
explicit developer-authorized handoff accepted by this bound replacement session under Protocol
parallel. Before editing read the exact approved plan/context and relevant code, state your
understanding and reconcile discrepancies. Reuse its
assigned worktree, and maintain lifecycle through `scripts/worker.py update`. Stop uncommitted
at the separate commit review gate; dispatch/resume never grants approval.
Address requirements, scope and approval questions directly to the developer here and pause;
only assignment/resource coordination belongs with the dispatcher.

Existing plans under `docs/agents/projects/<slug>.md` or `docs/agents/plans/<slug>.md`
remain valid inputs; continue using
the recorded path without moving another worker's file or resetting its approval gate.

$ARGUMENTS

lightweight.description: Small change without a plan, following docs/agents/protocols/lightweight.md
lightweight.template:
Follow `docs/agents/protocols/lightweight.md` exactly for this change:

For a registered worker, reuse its assigned worktree, maintain lifecycle through
`scripts/worker.py update`, and stop uncommitted at commit review in this worker session.
If planning is required, discuss requirements and obtain plan approval here before implementation.

$ARGUMENTS

plan.template:
Follow `docs/agents/protocols/plan.md` exactly for this change:

If this is a registered worker, reuse its assigned branch/worktree, maintain its lifecycle
through `scripts/worker.py update`, and discuss requirements and obtain approval here.
Address requirements, scope decisions and approvals directly to the developer in this visible
conversation and pause here; send only assignment/resource conflicts to the dispatcher.
At review include the implementation recommendation: continue this session by default, or a
specific available backend/model justified by remaining uncertainty, with escalation conditions.
Respect explicit developer preferences; dispatch chooses only the initial planning model.
Dispatch is not plan or commit approval.

$ARGUMENTS
